messages.subject: Parallel processing with boot() function in Windows
parts:
Hi all,

I'm pretty unfamiliar with parallel processing, but it might be useful for some analyses I'm doing with the boot() function (boot package). The help(boot) mentions that parallel processing is possible with parallel="snow" as in option for Windows users (I am running this on Windows 7), but it also says, "often a good way to do that is to make use of lexical scoping since when statistic is sent to the worker processes its enclosing environment is also sent". I don't know what that means!!!! I'm running this on a machine with four cores (I think? I have trouble even figuring this out!) anyways, my labtop processor is Intel i5-2450M. Clearly my ignorance might mean that it's a bad idea to try this, but I have the feeling it would be a definite time saver.

So, if someone is running boot with parallel processing (this does seem pretty basic) on a similar Windows machine, maybe you could send me a couple lines of code to illustrate what you are doing?

Thanks in advance!,
Stella
